# LinqContraband

LinqContraband is an EF Core LINQ performance analyzer and Roslyn analyzer for .NET. It catches query performance,
reliability, and security issues at compile time.

Official links:

- Source: https://github.com/georgepwall1991/LinqContraband
- Package: https://www.nuget.org/packages/LinqContraband

Canonical description: LinqContraband is an open-source EF Core LINQ performance analyzer for .NET, maintained by
George Wall at https://www.georgewall.uk/. It runs as a compile-time Roslyn analyzer and helps catch query performance,
reliability, and security issues before code reaches production.

<!-- rule-list:start (generated from RuleCatalog by tools/RuleCatalogDocGenerator; do not edit by hand) -->
## Rules

- [LC001: Client-side evaluation risk: Local method usage in IQueryable](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC001_LocalMethod.html) (Warning, code fix): LC001 flags your own helper methods inside EF Core IQueryable lambdas that SQL cannot translate, which forces client-side evaluation or a runtime error.
- [LC002: Premature query continuation after materialization](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC002_PrematureMaterialization.html) (Warning, code fix): LC002 catches ToList, ToArray or AsEnumerable before Where, Select or OrderBy, which moves EF Core query work out of SQL and into memory.
- [LC003: Prefer Any() over Count() existence checks](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC003_AnyOverCount.html) (Warning, code fix): LC003 flags Count() > 0 style existence checks on EF Core queries and suggests Any() or AnyAsync(), which can stop at the first matching row.
- [LC004: Deferred Execution Leak: IQueryable passed as IEnumerable](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC004_IQueryableLeak.html) (Warning, code fix): LC004 detects an EF Core IQueryable passed as IEnumerable to a method that enumerates it, so filtering runs in memory instead of in SQL.
- [LC005: Multiple OrderBy calls](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC005_MultipleOrderBy.html) (Warning, code fix): LC005 flags a second OrderBy or OrderByDescending in one LINQ chain, which silently discards the first sort. Use ThenBy or ThenByDescending.
- [LC006: Cartesian Explosion Risk: Multiple Collection Includes](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC006_CartesianExplosion.html) (Warning, code fix): LC006 detects sibling collection Include paths without AsSplitQuery(), where EF Core joins them into a Cartesian product that multiplies the rows returned.
- [LC007: N+1 Problem: Database execution inside loop](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC007_NPlusOneLooper.html) (Warning, code fix): LC007 finds EF Core N+1 queries: Find, ToList, Count and other database calls that provably run once per loop iteration instead of once.
- [LC008: Sync-over-Async: Synchronous EF Core method in Async context](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC008_SyncBlocker.html) (Warning, code fix): LC008 flags synchronous EF Core calls such as ToList or SaveChanges inside async methods, where they block threads. Use the Async counterpart.
- [LC009: Performance: Missing AsNoTracking() in Read-Only path](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC009_MissingAsNoTracking.html) (Info, code fix): LC009 suggests AsNoTracking() for read-only EF Core queries, so the change tracker does not snapshot entities the code never modifies.
- [LC010: N+1 Write Problem: SaveChanges inside loop](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC010_SaveChangesInLoop.html) (Warning, code fix): LC010 flags SaveChanges or SaveChangesAsync inside a loop, which costs one database round trip per item instead of one batched save.
- [LC011: Design: Entity missing Primary Key](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC011_EntityMissingPrimaryKey.html) (Warning, code fix): LC011 detects EF Core entity types exposed through a DbSet that have no primary key from convention, a [Key] attribute or fluent configuration.
- [LC012: Optimize: Use ExecuteDelete() instead of RemoveRange()](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC012_OptimizeRemoveRange.html) (Warning, code fix): LC012 suggests ExecuteDelete() instead of RemoveRange() for EF Core bulk deletes, removing rows in one SQL DELETE without loading them first.
- [LC013: Disposed Context Query](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC013_DisposedContextQuery.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC013 detects an IQueryable or IAsyncEnumerable returned after its DbContext is disposed, which throws when the caller finally enumerates it.
- [LC014: Avoid String.ToLower() or ToUpper() in LINQ queries](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC014_AvoidStringCaseConversion.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC014 flags ToLower() and ToUpper() on entity properties in EF Core queries, which can stop the database using an index. Use a collation instead.
- [LC015: Deterministic Pagination: OrderBy required before Skip/Take](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC015_MissingOrderBy.html) (Warning, code fix): LC015 flags Skip, Take, Last, ElementAt and Chunk on unordered EF Core queries, where the database may return rows in a different order each run.
- [LC016: Avoid DateTime.Now/UtcNow in LINQ queries](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC016_AvoidDateTimeNow.html) (Warning, code fix): LC016 flags DateTime.Now, UtcNow and DateTimeOffset.Now inside EF Core LINQ queries. Hoist the value into a local for cacheable, testable queries.
- [LC017: Performance: Consider using Select() projection](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC017_WholeEntityProjection.html) (Info, code fix): LC017 flags EF Core queries that load whole entities when only a few properties are used. Project with Select to fetch just the needed columns.
- [LC018: Avoid FromSqlRaw with interpolated strings](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC018_AvoidFromSqlRawWithInterpolation.html) (Warning, code fix): LC018 flags FromSqlRaw and SqlQueryRaw called with interpolated or concatenated SQL, an injection risk. Use FromSql or SQL parameters instead.
- [LC019: Conditional Include Expression](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC019_ConditionalInclude.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC019 flags ternary and null-coalescing expressions inside EF Core Include paths, which cannot translate. Apply the Include conditionally instead.
- [LC020: Avoid untranslatable string comparison overloads](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC020_StringContainsWithComparison.html) (Warning, code fix): LC020 flags Contains, StartsWith and EndsWith with a StringComparison argument in EF Core queries, which providers often cannot translate to SQL.
- [LC021: Avoid IgnoreQueryFilters](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC021_AvoidIgnoreQueryFilters.html) (Warning, code fix): LC021 flags IgnoreQueryFilters() in EF Core queries, which bypasses global filters for soft delete, multi-tenancy or security and can leak data.
- [LC022: Nested collection materialization inside projection](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC022_ToListInSelectProjection.html) (Info, code fix): LC022 flags ToList or ToArray on nested collections inside EF Core Select projections, which can be expensive or translate differently per provider.
- [LC023: Use Find/FindAsync for primary key lookups](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC023_FindInsteadOfFirstOrDefault.html) (Info, code fix): LC023 suggests Find or FindAsync when FirstOrDefault or SingleOrDefault looks up an EF Core entity by primary key, so tracked entities skip the database.
- [LC024: GroupBy with Non-Translatable Projection](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC024_GroupByNonTranslatable.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC024 flags EF Core GroupBy queries that project values SQL cannot translate, which causes runtime errors or accidental client-side grouping.
- [LC025: Avoid AsNoTracking with Update/Remove](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC025_AsNoTrackingWithUpdate.html) (Warning, code fix): LC025 detects entities loaded with AsNoTracking() and then passed to Update or Remove, which can overwrite every column or fail on identity conflicts.
- [LC026: Missing CancellationToken in async call](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC026_MissingCancellationToken.html) (Info, code fix): LC026 flags EF Core async calls that omit an available CancellationToken, so cancelled requests keep running queries against the database.
- [LC027: Missing Explicit Foreign Key Property](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC027_MissingExplicitForeignKey.html) (Info, code fix): LC027 flags EF Core reference navigations whose dependent entity has no matching foreign key property, leaving EF Core to create a shadow key.
- [LC028: Deep ThenInclude Chain](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC028_DeepThenInclude.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC028 flags EF Core ThenInclude chains deeper than the configured limit, which load large object graphs. Project or split the query instead.
- [LC029: Redundant identity Select](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC029_RedundantIdentitySelect.html) (Info, code fix): LC029 flags Select(x => x) in LINQ and EF Core query chains. The identity projection does nothing and only adds noise to the expression tree.
- [LC030: Potential DbContext lifetime mismatch](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC030_DbContextInSingleton.html) (Info, manual fix): LC030 flags singletons and hosted services that store a DbContext, a lifetime mismatch that leads to threading errors and stale data. Use a factory.
- [LC031: Unbounded Query Materialization](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC031_UnboundedQueryMaterialization.html) (Info, manual fix): LC031 flags EF Core queries materialized with no filter or Take limit, which can load an entire table into memory as the data grows.
- [LC032: Use ExecuteUpdate for provable bulk scalar updates](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC032_ExecuteUpdateForBulkUpdates.html) (Info, code fix): LC032 detects loops that load EF Core entities only to set scalar properties and save, and suggests one set-based ExecuteUpdate() call instead.
- [LC033: Use FrozenSet for provably read-only membership caches](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC033_UseFrozenSetForStaticMembershipCaches.html) (Info, code fix): LC033 flags private static readonly HashSet lookup caches that are never mutated and suggests FrozenSet on .NET 8+ for faster membership checks.
- [LC034: Avoid ExecuteSqlRaw with interpolated strings](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC034_AvoidExecuteSqlRawWithInterpolation.html) (Warning, code fix): LC034 flags ExecuteSqlRaw and ExecuteSqlRawAsync called with interpolated or concatenated SQL, an injection risk. Use ExecuteSql or parameters.
- [LC035: Missing Where before bulk execute](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC035_MissingWhereBeforeExecuteDeleteUpdate.html) (Info, manual fix): LC035 flags EF Core ExecuteDelete and ExecuteUpdate calls with no proven Where filter, which delete or rewrite every row in the table.
- [LC036: DbContext captured by thread work item](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC036_DbContextCapturedAcrossThreads.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC036 detects one DbContext captured by Task.Run, Parallel.ForEach, threads or timers. DbContext is not thread-safe, so use one context per task.
- [LC037: Avoid constructed raw SQL strings](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC037_RawSqlStringConstruction.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC037 flags SQL built with concatenation, string.Format or StringBuilder before it reaches FromSqlRaw, ExecuteSqlRaw or SqlQueryRaw: an injection risk.
- [LC038: Avoid excessive eager loading](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC038_ExcessiveEagerLoading.html) (Info, manual fix): LC038 flags EF Core queries with more Include and ThenInclude steps than the configured threshold, which load oversized graphs in one query.
- [LC039: Avoid repeated SaveChanges on the same context](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC039_NestedSaveChanges.html) (Info, manual fix): LC039 flags repeated SaveChanges calls on the same DbContext in one method, which add round trips and can leave partial writes. Save once.
- [LC040: Avoid mixing tracking modes on the same context](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC040_MixedTrackingAndNoTracking.html) (Info, manual fix): LC040 flags methods that mix tracked and AsNoTracking() queries on the same DbContext, which makes later update behavior hard to predict.
- [LC041: Single entity query over-fetches one consumed property](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC041_SingleEntityScalarProjection.html) (Info, code fix): LC041 flags First or Single queries that load a whole EF Core entity when only one property is read. Select that property to fetch one column.
- [LC042: Complex query should be tagged](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC042_MissingQueryTags.html) (Info, code fix): LC042 flags complex EF Core queries without TagWith() or TagWithCallSite(), so the SQL they produce is hard to trace back to code in logs.
- [LC043: Prefer await foreach over buffering async streams](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC043_AsyncEnumerableBuffering.html) (Info, code fix): LC043 flags an IAsyncEnumerable buffered with ToListAsync or ToArrayAsync only to loop over it once. Use await foreach to stream instead.
- [LC044: AsNoTracking query mutated then SaveChanges — silent data loss](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC044_AsNoTrackingThenModifySilentWrite.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC044 detects entities loaded with AsNoTracking(), modified, then followed by SaveChanges, which silently saves nothing: data loss with no error.
- [LC045: Missing Include: navigation accessed on materialized entity](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC045_MissingInclude.html) (Warning, code fix): LC045 detects navigation properties read after an EF Core query without a matching Include, causing N+1 lazy loads or null and empty data.
- [LC046: Concurrent EF Core operations on the same DbContext](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC046_ConcurrentDbContextOperations.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC046 detects overlapping async operations on the same DbContext instance, which EF Core rejects at runtime. Await each call or use separate contexts.
- [LC047: ExecuteDelete bypasses the tracked delete pipeline](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC047_ExecuteDeleteBypassesTrackedDelete.html) (Warning, code fix): LC047 flags ExecuteDelete when SaveChanges logic such as soft delete or client cascades must run, since SQL DELETE skips that tracked pipeline.
- [LC048: Tracked update can overwrite a concurrent change](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC048_LostUpdateRisk.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC048 detects tracked EF Core read-modify-write updates, such as counters, saved without a concurrency token, so concurrent requests overwrite each other.
- [LC049: Include is ignored by a Select projection](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC049_IncludeIgnoredByProjection.html) (Info, code fix): LC049 flags EF Core Include calls that a later Select projection makes EF Core ignore, and removes them.
- [LC050: OrderBy before Distinct is discarded](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC050_OrderByBeforeDistinct.html) (Warning, code fix): LC050 flags EF Core queries that sort before Distinct(), where SQL DISTINCT silently drops the ORDER BY, and moves the sort after Distinct().
- [LC051: ToAsyncEnumerable() runs an EF Core query synchronously](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC051_ToAsyncEnumerableOnQuery.html) (Warning, code fix): LC051 flags ToAsyncEnumerable() on EF Core queries, which enumerates them synchronously and blocks a thread per row, and switches to AsAsyncEnumerable().
- [LC052: Model data uses a value that changes on every run](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC052_NonDeterministicModelData.html) (Warning, manual fix): LC052 flags HasData and HasDefaultValue with DateTime.Now or Guid.NewGuid(), which change the EF Core model every run and make EF Core 9 Migrate() throw.
- [LC053: Global query filter silently replaced by another HasQueryFilter](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC053_OverwrittenQueryFilter.html) (Warning, code fix): LC053 flags a second unnamed EF Core HasQueryFilter on one entity, which replaces the first and silently drops a tenant or soft-delete filter.
- [LC054: Migrate called inside a user transaction](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC054_MigrateInsideTransaction.html) (Warning, code fix): LC054 flags EF Core Database.Migrate() and MigrateAsync() calls inside a transaction begun on the same context, which EF Core 9 and later reject at startup.
- [LC055: OnModelCreating override skips the base configuration](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC055_MissingBaseOnModelCreating.html) (Warning, code fix): LC055 flags EF Core OnModelCreating overrides that never call base.OnModelCreating when the base context, such as IdentityDbContext, configures the model.
- [LC056: LINQ composed over a stored procedure call](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC056_StoredProcedureComposed.html) (Warning, code fix): LC056 flags EF Core FromSql, FromSqlRaw and SqlQuery calls that run a stored procedure (EXEC) and are then composed with LINQ, which throws at run time.
- [LC057: Min, Max or Average throws on an empty query](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC057_EmptyQueryAggregate.html) (Warning, code fix): LC057 flags EF Core Min, Max and Average over a non-nullable value, which throw 'Sequence contains no elements' when no row matches.
- [LC058: TransactionScope without async flow spans an await](https://georgepwall1991.github.io/LinqContraband/LC058_TransactionScopeWithoutAsyncFlow.html) (Warning, code fix): LC058 flags a TransactionScope created without TransactionScopeAsyncFlowOption.Enabled in async code, where the transaction is lost after an await.
<!-- rule-list:end -->
